content: Recently, the CI of repository https://github.com/acmepjz/lean-iwasawa is not working. Lean action failed with "'git' exited with code 128". Regarding the error log https://github.com/acmepjz/lean-iwasawa/actions/runs/23628341628/job/68822087476 it seems that it's failed to checkout https://github.com/dupuisf/BibtexQuery. But the git repository and revision seems correct. A Google search does not find useful information. What should I do now?

I remember other people had this issue and bumping mathlib seemed to fix it:

  • #lean4 > UnicodeBasic: 'git' exited with code 128
  • #combinatorial-games > GitHub actions @ 💬

@Mac Malone I thought we had reached a point that lake never failed because of a git error without actually surfacing that error message to the user? Is this a regression? We really need to make sure we always surface the error messages.

OK after lake update the github CI works (module old code not adapted to new mathlib). But it then breaks on my local computer.

At first lake update (as well as lake exe cache get) complain that the Plausible package has conflict revision in my project vs in mathlib. So I overwrite the revision in my project using that of mathlib.

Then lake exe cache get complains that failed to fetch ProofWidgets binary (which almost 100% happen in China mainland due to network restriction, the common solution is run lake exe cache get again). By running lake exe cache get again, it does not complain anymore, and caches are downloaded successfully.

Then in VSCode it complains that the mathlib cache is outdated and needs rebuild :exploding_head: And lake build failed with the following error:

[524/550] Building proofwidgets/widgetJsAll
error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date. Please run `lake exe cache get` to fetch the latest ProofWidgets. If this does not work, report your issue on the Lean Zulip.
Some required targets logged failures:
- proofwidgets/widgetJsAll
error: build failed

And running lake exe cache get does not fetch ProofWidgets, instead, it shows

Current branch: HEAD
Using cache (Azure) from origin: leanprover-community/mathlib4
No files to download
Already decompressed 8205 file(s)

What should I do now? How can I fetch ProofWidgets manually?

[EDIT] After I run lake clean && lake exe cache get, I got the following error message:

lake stdout:
✔ [0/2] Ran job computation
✖ [1/2] (Optional) Fetching proofwidgets:optRelease
trace: .> curl -s -S -f -o C:\Users\***\Documents\projects\lean-iwasawa\.lake\packages\proofwidgets\.lake\ProofWidgets4.tar.gz -L https://github.com/leanprover-community/ProofWidgets4/releases/download/v0.0.94/ProofWidgets4.tar.gz
trace: .> tar -xvvz -f C:\Users\***\Documents\projects\lean-iwasawa\.lake\packages\proofwidgets\.lake\ProofWidgets4.tar.gz -C C:\Users\***\Documents\projects\lean-iwasawa\.lake\packages\proofwidgets\.lake\build
error: failed to execute 'tar': Tried to read from handle containing non UTF-8 data.
✖ [2/2] Running proofwidgets:release
error: failed to fetch GitHub release (see 'proofwidgets:optRelease' for details)
Some required targets logged failures:
- proofwidgets:release
lake stderr:
error: build failed
Fetching ProofWidgets cloud release...
uncaught exception: Failed to fetch ProofWidgets cloud release: lake failed with error code 1

I've checked that the file ProofWidgets4.tar.gz was downloaded successfully, but somehow tar command was running wrong. I tried re-run such command manually on another terminal, it unpacked successfully. So I think somehow there was something wrong in the ProofWidgets binary unpacking script on Windows.

Kim Morrison said:

Mac Malone I thought we had reached a point that lake never failed because of a git error without actually surfacing that error message to the user? Is this a regression? We really need to make sure we always surface the error messages.

Lake does log Git errors when Git fails, but Git does not always produce an error message when it fails.
(Though, also, Lake does sometimes need to be run with -v to surface Git logs.)
Since I was looking at the code, I made lean4#13151 to remove one situation where -v would be necessary. I'll see if it breaks any tests in a significant way.

Jz Pan said:

I've checked that the file ProofWidgets4.tar.gz was downloaded successfully, but somehow tar command was running wrong. I tried re-run such command manually on another terminal, it unpacked successfully. So I think somehow there was something wrong in the ProofWidgets binary unpacking script on Windows.

Does your user name contain non-ASCII characters? If so, perhaps something got confused on Windows when attempting to spawn tar with a path argument contained non-ASCII characters.

Mac Malone said:

Jz Pan said:

I've checked that the file ProofWidgets4.tar.gz was downloaded successfully, but somehow tar command was running wrong. I tried re-run such command manually on another terminal, it unpacked successfully. So I think somehow there was something wrong in the ProofWidgets binary unpacking script on Windows.

Does your user name contain non-ASCII characters? If so, perhaps something got confused on Windows when attempting to spawn tar with a path argument contained non-ASCII characters.

No, my $HOME path only contains English alphabet and _.

Now I've unpacked ProofWidgets4.tar.gz manually, but lake build or lake build proofwidgets still complains that ProofWidgets not up-to-date. How can I convince the builder that it is already up to date?
@Jz Pan Ah, in that case, this sounds like the problem discussd in #general > ProofWidgets not up-to-date @ 💬 .
Thank you! It fixed by deleting all cache and update again.
